get.description: Over `from` to `to`, project-local days both included (default the 28 days ending today; at most 92, `422 window_too_large`). Each cell counts valid, current answers: `numerator` of `denominator`, with `n_observations` every answer of the cell and `value` null when the denominator is 0. Share of voice is doc 16 section 5 per observation: the own brand's share of the tracked entities each answer names, over the answers that name one; the response lists the entity set once. Branded prompts are left out unless `include_branded` is true; `branded_only` keeps them alone. A prompt of two topics counts in both; prompts without a topic share a row with `term_id` null. `filter[country_iso]` keeps the prompts of one market and `filter[term]` the prompts given the term or one under it; the topic rows then hold only those prompts, and under `filter[term]` they are the term and the topics below it, with no row for prompts without a topic. Each row says when its last counted answer and its last valid one came. `include=series` adds a point for each week the window touches (weeks start on Monday in the project's timezone), with Mentioned, Cited and Share of voice over the week's answers. The first and last weeks may be partial (cut at the window bounds; the first `week_start` can precede `window.from`). A point of a prompt row always holds the trailing four weeks to its week, and one of a topic, total or country row does when fewer than 10 of its prompts answered that week (`is_pooled`, `pool`, `prompts`): a pooled point never reaches outside the window, so the first points hold fewer weeks, and the points of a prompt row do not add up to its window cell. `include=entities` adds, per engine, a Mentioned and a Share of voice cell for each tracked entity (the own ones first, at most 20); across all the entities an answer names, its shares add up to 1. With `include=series` too, each point also holds those cells over the very weeks the point holds (its own week, or the weeks it pools), as `entities`, without `previous`. `compare=previous_period` (as many days just before the window), `compare=previous_year` (the same dates a year earlier; 29 February becomes the 28th) or `compare_from` with `compare_to` (both or neither, at most 92 days, any position; they win over `compare`) add `compare_window` and `previous_answers` (the valid answers in scope there), and `previous` beside each engine's cells, and beside each entity's with `include=entities`: null when none of the row's prompts has an answer of the engine in that window, cells with a denominator of 0 when it has answers and none valid. `include=total` adds `total`: every prompt in scope as one row, aggregated as a topic row is, with the `previous`, `series` and `entities` blocks when asked. `rows=topics` leaves the prompt rows out and `rows=none` both row lists; `total` does not depend on `rows`. `include=co_mentions` adds `co_mentions`: per engine shown, the valid answers in scope and, for each pair of the tracked entities (the own ones first, at most 20) named in the same valid answer, how many answers name both; it does not depend on `rows`. `include=cells` adds `detail` to every engine of the rows, `total` and `by_country`: Cited among the answers with citations, the own share of the citation units, First mention (the own brand named before any other tracked entity, of the answers that name it) and the fan-out presence and mean (null on an engine that does not expose fan-out), over the window alone, with `metric_context.detail`. Blocks not asked for are left out. `filter[outcome]=O` keeps a prompt row when at least one of its valid answers in the window, on the engines shown, had outcome O; `filter[opportunity]` keeps it by the same rule: `named_not_cited` is outcome `mentioned_only`, `cited_not_named` is `cited_only`, `nobody_named` is no tracked entity named, `lost_to:<entity_id>` is that competitor named and the own brand not (an id that is not a competitor of the project keeps no row and is not an error). With both, a row must pass each. They narrow `prompts` only: cells, topic rows, `total`, `co_mentions` and `prompt_count` still count every prompt in scope. `group_by=country` adds `by_country`: one entry per market of the prompts in scope (the prompt's own, sorted by code), with the engines built as a topic row of those prompts and the blocks the rows carry when asked; a prompt without a market is in no entry, and the block does not depend on `rows`, the outcome or opportunity filters.

The competitor and leading rules carry a span; the others carry none. Every result has `suggested_prompt_type`, the type the wording rule gives the text. With `items`, `estimate` says what the prompts that would be created cost on the standard queue, for each of `engine_codes` or, left out, each engine the project has on: the prompts the engine takes, the answers a month at two runs a week (rounded down), the cost a month to the cent, and the answers and cost of one run now.
